land.text: the Jingnan circuit round Jingzhou (Jiangling), held by Gao Jichang, 'a former general of Liang'

predecessors.note: Five Dynasties page: 'Jingnan (924-963) was founded by Gao Jichang, a former general of Liang'; 'Gao's successors claimed the title of King of Nanping after the fall of the Later Liang in 924'.
The Jingnan infobox says 'Preceded by: Later Tang'.

land.text: the Jingnan realm, overrun in 963: 'When the Song army was passing through the Jingnan, it easily took control of the capital city of Jingnan, Jiangling'

capitals.name: Jingzhou (Jiangling)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Jingzhou'; the Gao Jichong page names the capital Jiangling, the Jingzhou seat.

rulers.name: Gao Jixing (Prince Wuxin)
rulers.note: The infobox gives 909-928: he held the circuit from 909 (as Gao Jichang in the Five Dynasties page); the Jingnan state is dated from 924.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 926 shape unchanged, valid from the founding in 924

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 924-925 (Cliopatria starts the state in 926): infobox 'Established: 924'; the Five Dynasties page has the Nanping title claimed after the Later Liang fell in 924. The pages give no extent beyond the capital Jingzhou ('located in south-central China'), so the 926 outline is kept and unverified. Cliopatria's Later Liang shape for 911-925 may still contain this land; the later-liang-dynasty dossier does not cut it.

71,678 km2 round Jingzhou and the middle Yangtze. Unverified: the Jingnan page gives no extent and no area (Area: not stated), and the Gao Jichong page only 'its capital, Jiangling'; budget 1-2 pages.
71,055 km2, the 926 outline less a sliver of 623 km2 that no opened page explains (the Jingnan page records no territorial change 924-962). Valid 936-961.

Cliopatria runs the row to 969, six years past the end: Gao Jichong's country was 'overrun by Northern Song forces with little resistance' in 963 and the Jingnan infobox says 'Ended by the Song dynasty: 963'. 964-969 is Song land. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 962..963 from this entry's own 'valid 962-963 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: the Jingnan circuit round Jingzhou in south-central China

ledger.note: 924: the Gao family's Jingnan, or Nanping, begins at Jingzhou. Infobox 'Established: 924', 'Lasting from 924 to 963, it was located in south-central China'; the Five Dynasties page: 'Gao's successors claimed the title of King of Nanping after the fall of the Later Liang in 924'. The extent is Cliopatria's; no page gives the prefectures.

region.text: the Jingnan realm with its capital Jiangling

ledger.note: 963: the Song take Jiangling without a fight. 'When the Song army was passing through the Jingnan, it easily took control of the capital city of Jingnan, Jiangling'; Gao Jichong 'ordered his forces to surrender immediately'. The campaign was aimed at Wuping, where Zhou Xingfeng had died in 962 and Zhang Wenbiao rebelled. The page gives no month.

wars.name: Song conquest of Jingnan and Wuping
wars.outcome: Song troops sent after the Wuping rebellion of 962 passed through Jingnan, took Jiangling in 963 and received Gao Jichong's surrender; the country was 'overrun ... with little resistance'.
wars.note: The Five Dynasties page: 'Jingnan and Wuping Jiedushi were swept away in 963'. The whole state changed hands, so no contest zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The state is known by its capital Jingzhou and Cliopatria's outline; no page gives prefectures or a frontier with the Later Tang, Ma Chu, the Later Shu or the Southern Tang.

notes: Cliopatria row Jingnan 926-969 (3 shapes, 71,678 / 71,055 / 71,055 km2). The state is 924-963: the Jingnan infobox gives 'Established 924' and 'Ended 963', the Five Dynasties page 924-963, so Cliopatria's start is two years late and its end six years late. The three shapes are one outline (the 936 shape is 623 km2 smaller than the 926 one for no recorded reason). The extent is unverified: the three pages opened (a stub, a biography and the overview) give only the capital Jingzhou/Jiangling; the shape is kept with verdict ok and a note; no dedicated page on the Song conquest of Jingnan and Wuping was opened. Names: 'Jingnan' (荆南, the Gao family's state in Hubei) is a different thing from the Qi's Jingnan Circuit (靜難, Xianyang in Shaanxi) that the later-liang-dynasty dossier mentions. The Jingnan page names the founder Gao Jixing, the Five Dynasties page Gao Jichang; both are the same man, who held the circuit from 909 (infobox). Nominal ties are not drawn as vassal tints: the Five Dynasties page says Jingnan 'tried to maintain good relations with each of the Five Dynasties' and the Gao Jichong page has the Song appoint Gao Jichong jiedushi in 962 as a ceremony while Jingnan 'remained de facto independent'. Counterparts needing dossiers: Wuping circuit (Zhou Xingfeng 956-962, Zhou Baoquan, Zhang Wenbiao's rebellion; suggested slug wuping-circuit, already requested by the southern-chu dossier). Infobox area absent, so no ratio against 71,678 km2. Pages opened: three against a budget of one to two (one is the shared overview).
